payload.name: Relational-role to meeting-event retrieval
payload.description: When a question asks when a subject first met a person identified only by a relational role (future wife, fiancée, partner, spouse) and direct role-based hits are missing, apply this retrieval pattern.
content: Before answering 'no information,' when the question uses a relational role label for a person, expand searches to include meeting/encounter verbs (met, met up, went on a trip/date with) and descriptive terms from other memories that could identify that person (nationality, names, attributes).

If a later relationship memory is found (marriage, engagement, pregnancy, partner status), use it to identify the person, then search for the earliest meeting or trip event before that memory's date and report that event's time as the meeting.
Only a memory that explicitly describes the meeting or first encounter can establish the meeting time; do not infer it from the later relationship event alone.

solves: When a question identifies a person only by a relational role (future wife, spouse) and direct role-based retrieval fails, stored memories may describe the meeting by other attributes (nationality, trip partner). Expand retrieval to meeting/encounter terms and person descriptors, then chain from later relationship events to the earliest meeting. Do not infer meeting time from later relationship events alone.
